newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian welfare talks to go beyond Sept 30 - Fossa.
newsitem.headline: Italian welfare talks to go beyond Sept 30 - Fossa.

text.p: Negotations aimed at reforming the Italian welfare state will have to go on beyond the end of September, Giorgio Fossa, chairman of industrialists' organisation Confindustria, said on Tuesday.
The Italian government opened talks with unions and business leaders last week and hopes to reach a deal by September 30, when it wants to include details of the reform in the 1998 budget package.
But Fossa said more time was needed.
"No-one can delude themselves that a definitive reform of the welfare state can be concluded by September 30," Fossa said in a speech at a Confindustria presentation.
"The talks will have to go on for longer to give our country an economic platform from which to grow and not an economy which hides and folds in on itself," he said.

Earlier Confindustria said the government would have to find savings of 9.6 trillion lire in 1998 if it wanted to achieve its goal of keeping the ratio between social spending and gross domestic product to 1996/97 levels.
Social spending was 19.4 percent of GDP in that period, but is set to rise largely because of a growing pension bill. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
